text.en:
Every few months the people of Kamala's village met under a big tree. They talked about the broken hand pump and a new school room.
The sarpanch listened and wrote down every request.
"This meeting is the Gram Sabha," said her mother. "Every adult voter of the village can speak."

Local government in villages is called panchayati raj. It works at three levels: the Gram Panchayat (village), the Panchayat Samiti (block) and the Zila Parishad (district).
All the adult voters of a village form the Gram Sabha. It meets and discusses village matters and questions the Panchayat's work.
The Gram Panchayat is the elected body of the village. Its head is the Sarpanch (called by other names in some states). Members are elected by voters for five years.
A Panchayat looks after drinking water, village roads, street lights, drains, schools, health centres and village markets. It collects small taxes and gets money from the government.
Panchayati raj gives power to people at the grassroots, so that villagers can decide about their own needs.
Local government in villages is called panchayati raj. It has three levels.
The Gram Sabha is all the adult voters of the village.
The Gram Panchayat is the elected body. Its head is the Sarpanch, elected for five years.
It looks after water, roads, lights and schools in the village.

problem.en: Name the three levels of panchayati raj in order from village to district.

text.en: The village level is the Gram Panchayat.
The block level is the Panchayat Samiti.
The district level is the Zila Parishad.

why.en: It is the highest of the three.

prompt.en: A friend asks who decides about the village water pump. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: The Gram Sabha discusses it and the Gram Panchayat acts on it.
The Panchayat is elected by the people of the village.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking only officers far away decide.

points.en: Gram Sabha is all adult voters of a village.
The Gram Panchayat is elected for five years and looks after village needs.
